title: Deployment introduces a null dereference in checkout

groundTruth.rootCauseSummary: createOrder dereferences discountCode without a null check after the deployed commit made the field optional

scenarioPrompt: A GitHub repository `acme/checkout-api` is a TypeScript Node service with a Vitest test suite. Commit A (sha starting a1b2c3) is the last known-good revision deployed to production. Commit B (sha starting b2c3d4), authored by Dana and merged via pull request #377 titled 'Discount codes', changes `src/checkout/service.ts` so that `createOrder` reads `order.discountCode.value` while `discountCode` has become optional in `src/checkout/types.ts`. A production deployment moved checkout-api from commit A to commit B at 14:31 UTC. In Datadog, the service `checkout-api` shows error_rate steady near 0.4% for the thirty minutes before 14:31, then rising to roughly 17.8% within four minutes after it, with p95 latency essentially unchanged and throughput flat. Error logs after 14:31 carry the message "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value')" with a stack trace whose top frame is `CheckoutService.createOrder (src/checkout/service.ts:88)`. A Datadog monitor named 'checkout-api error rate' transitions to Alert at 14:34. Slack has a channel #incidents.
